provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Phonics: q and r words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say q and r words.
The pupils should be able to point to q and r pictures.

Introduction:
We have learned many sounds. Today we learn q and r sounds.
These sounds are in words we use every day.

Content:
Q is for queen. A queen wears a crown.
Q is for quilt. A quilt keeps us warm at night.
R is for rat. A rat is a small animal.
R is for rain. Rain falls from the sky.

Class activity:
Show pictures of queen, quilt, rat, and rain.
Pupils say each word and point to the picture.

Evaluation questions:
What sound does queen begin with?
What sound does rain begin with?
Point to the rat picture.

Summary:
We can say and point to q and r words.

topics.title: Phonics: s and t words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say s and t words.
The pupils should be able to match s and t words to pictures.

Introduction:
Last week we learned q and r sounds.
This week we learn s and t sounds.

Content:
S is for sun. The sun gives us light.
S is for sit. We sit on chairs.
T is for top. A top spins around.
T is for tap. Water comes from a tap.

Class activity:
Show objects like a toy top and a picture of a tap.
Pupils say each word and pass the objects around.

Evaluation questions:
What sound does sun begin with?
What sound does top begin with?
Show me how to sit.

Summary:
We can say and match s and t words.

topics.title: Phonics: u to z words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say u to z words.
The pupils should be able to identify u to z letters.

Introduction:
We have learned many sounds so far.
Today we learn sounds from u to z.

Content:
U is for umbrella. An umbrella keeps us dry in rain.
V is for van. A van is a big vehicle.
W is for wet. Wet clothes need sun to dry.
Y is for yam. Yam is a food we eat.
Z is for zebra. A zebra has black and white stripes.

Class activity:
Show pictures of umbrella, van, wet things, yam, and zebra.
Pupils say each word and make the first sound.

Evaluation questions:
What sound does umbrella begin with?
What sound does zebra begin with?
Point to something wet in the classroom.

Summary:
We can say and identify u to z words.

topics.title: Simple sentences about self
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say their name.
The pupils should be able to say if they are a boy or girl.

Introduction:
We all have names and we are boys or girls.
Today we learn to say sentences about ourselves.

Content:
My name is [pupil's name].
I am a boy.
I am a girl.
We say these sentences when we meet new people.

Class activity:
Each pupil stands up and says their name.
Then they say if they are a boy or girl.
The class claps for each pupil.

Evaluation questions:
What is your name?
Are you a boy or girl?
Say a sentence about yourself.

Summary:
We can say simple sentences about ourselves.

topics.title: Comprehension: my family
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to talk about their family.
The pupils should be able to answer simple questions about family.

Introduction:
All of us have families that love us.
Today we learn to talk about our families.

Content:
Family means the people who live with you.
You have mother, father, brother, sister.
You can say I love my family.
You can say my family is big or small.

Class activity:
Bring family photos if possible.
Pupils take turns to talk about who is in their family.

Evaluation questions:
Who is in your family?
Is your family big or small?
Do you love your family?

Summary:
We can talk about our families.

topics.title: Story time
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to listen to a story.
The pupils should be able to retell a story in their own words.

Introduction:
Stories help us learn new things.
Today we will listen to a story and then tell it ourselves.

Content:
Listen carefully to the teacher.
Remember the beginning, middle and end.
Use your own words to tell the story.
Speak clearly so everyone can hear you.

Class activity:
Teacher tells a short story about a boy who helps his mother.
Pupils sit in a circle and each says one sentence about the story.

Evaluation questions:
What was the story about?
Who was the main character?
What happened at the end?

Summary:
We can listen and retell stories.

topics.title: Writing: capital letters U to Z
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write capital letters U to Z.
The pupils should be able to say each letter name.

Introduction:
We have learned many letters so far.
Today we learn to write capital letters U to Z.

Content:
U is written like a cup with a handle.
V is written like a valley with two sides.
W is written like two V's together.
X is made with two crossing lines.
Y is like a V with a tail.
Z is written with a line across the middle.

Class activity:
Pupils trace the letters in the air with their fingers.
Then they trace the letters on sand or a board.

Evaluation questions:
Show me how to write U.
What comes after W in the alphabet?
Say all the letters from U to Z.

Summary:
We can write capital letters U to Z.

topics.title: Writing: small letters k to z
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write small letters k to z.
The pupils should be able to match small letters to capital letters.

Introduction:
Last week we wrote capital letters.
This week we learn small letters k to z.

Content:
Small k has a straight line with a leg.
Small l is just a straight line.
Small m has two humps.
Small n has one hump.
Small o is a circle.
Small p has a straight line with a tail.

Class activity:
Pupils write each small letter in their notebooks.
Then they match each small letter to its capital letter.

Evaluation questions:
Show me how to write small m.
Which small letter looks like a circle?
Match small k to capital K.

Summary:
We can write small letters k to z.

topics.title: Talking: greetings and manners
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say greetings properly.
The pupils should be able to use thank you and please.

Introduction:
When we meet people, we should be polite.
Today we learn how to greet people and be polite.

Content:
Good morning is a greeting for daytime.
Good afternoon is for later in the day.
Good evening is for when the sun is setting.
Thank you shows you are grateful.
Please shows you are polite.

Class activity:
Pupils practice greeting each other in pairs.
One pupil says good morning, the other responds.
They practice saying please and thank you.

Evaluation questions:
What do you say when you meet your teacher?
When do you say thank you?
Show me how to greet a friend.

Summary:
We can greet people politely and use manners.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall what we learned this year.
The pupils should be able to answer questions about all topics.

Introduction:
We have learned many things in English this year.
Today we will review all we have learned.

Content:
We learned phonics from a to z.
We learned to write capital and small letters.
We learned to make simple sentences.
We learned to talk about our family.
We learned to listen and tell stories.
We learned greetings and manners.

Class activity:
The teacher asks questions about all topics.
Pupils raise hands to answer.
The class sings the alphabet song together.

Evaluation questions:
What sound does zebra begin with?
How do you greet your teacher?
Write the letter A.
Tell me about your family.

Summary:
We have learned many things in English this year.
